懐.meaning: Before launch, an astronaut stitches a little <part>net</part> into her space <part>garment</part>, right over her <part>heartbeat</part>, and stuffs it with <part>ten</part> jelly beans. Mission control never finds out. Floating past the moon, she reaches into her secret <kanji>pocket</kanji>.
懐.on: Back on Earth she finds one more thing in there: a tiny folded <sound>ki</sound>te, which she flies over the launch pad.
懐.kun: The last jelly bean rolls out onto her <sound>fu</sound>ton, past a toy <sound>to</sound>tem pole, a <sound>ko</sound>ala keyring and a <sound>ro</sound>cket sticker.

析.meaning: A detective suspects a garden <part>tree</part> of hiding a stolen ring, so he takes a tiny silver <part>axe</part> and splits it into slices thin as paper, studying each one through his magnifying glass. No ring, just a squirrel's diary. Every clue gets the same treatment: <kanji>chop</kanji>, then look.
析.on: He lays the slices out on the lawn like a pie chart, one <sound>sec</sound>tor for each branch.

膨.meaning: Every time a tomcat hears the <part>drum</part> at the harvest fair, he gulps air with excitement. His belly puffs up, his <part>whiskers</part> stick straight out, and by the last song he's round as the full <part>moon</part> and floating over the tents. Music makes him <kanji>swell</kanji>.
膨.on: At last he bumps down on a mossy <sound>bou</sound>lder with a soft pop and rolls off it, purring.
膨.kun: He drifts over a <sound>fu</sound>ton stall and a <sound>coo</sound>k flipping pancakes, still getting rounder.

抵.meaning: The husky team strains at the <part>sled</part>, but a penguin who hates leaving home has dropped a ship's <part>anchor</part> through the ice behind it. The dogs pull, the penguin folds its flippers, and the sled doesn't budge an inch. He will <kanji>resist</kanji> any trip.
抵.on: The dogs try to <sound>ta</sound>pe the anchor chain to a post, but the penguin peels the tape off.

旨.meaning: A dragon at breakfast scoops up the morning <part>sun</part> with a big silver <part>spoon</part>, blows on it and swallows it whole. The sky goes dark for a moment, then he burps out a rainbow. 'Warm, sweet and crunchy,' he sighs. Totally <kanji>delicious</kanji>.
旨.on: His knight friend holds up a <sound>shi</sound>eld against the hot burp, just in case.
旨.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se at the next table catches the falling crumbs of sunshine in a <sound>ne</sound>t.

希.meaning: A castaway on a tiny island cuts his last <part>cloth</part> shirt into big letters with rusty <part>scissors</part>: H, E, L, P. A seagull steals the P, and a plane flies over waving. He snips the letters again anyway. He never runs out of <kanji>hope</kanji>.
希.on: Next he cuts a <sound>key</sound> out of the scraps, in case a door ever washes up.
希.kun: Once in a blue moon, a <sound>ma</sound>ma whale in a <sound>re</sound>d bucket hat swims past his island: rare.

誓.meaning: Two paper cranes get married. Each writes its wedding <part>speech</part> on its own wing, then they <part>fold</part> the wings together so the words touch for good. No take-backs now. Folded paper keeps a <kanji>vow</kanji>.
誓.on: The folded wings are locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe until their golden anniversary.
誓.kun: The best man, a <sound>chee</sound>tah, swears loyalty too, with one paw on a <sound>ca</sound>rp-shaped cake.

譲.meaning: Two roommates face a <part>laundry pile</part> as high as the fridge. Each gives a polite <part>speech</part>: 'After you.' 'No, after you.' They bow and wave for a week while the pile reaches the ceiling. Neither will be rude, so both <kanji>defer</kanji>.
譲.on: In the end a <sound>jo</sound>ey hops in from next door and folds the whole pile.
譲.kun: At breakfast one roommate holds out the last <sound>yuzu</sound> on a plate: 'You have it.'

購.meaning: A crab builds tall <part>scaffolding</part> next to his sandcastle and pays the postman one <part>shellfish</part> shell a week, so a fresh comic is dropped on top every Monday. The tower grows by one comic a week. It's the longest <kanji>subscription</kanji> on the beach.
購.on: The postman always brings him an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne too, as a thank-you.

烈.meaning: Fans line up in a <part>rank</part> and walk barefoot across <part>hot coals</part> just to get a goldfish's autograph. They cheer the whole way and nobody even says ouch. The goldfish signs each fin-print with a bubble. Now that's <kanji>ardent</kanji>.
烈.on: Afterwards they all raise a little glass of <sound>rets</sound>ina to the goldfish.
烈.kun: One fan in a <sound>ha</sound>rp-shaped hat yells so hard that a <sound>ge</sound>cko falls off the wall.

猛.meaning: A little <part>child</part> guards the last cookie on the <part>dish</part> with a toy <part>fishhook</part>, growling at anyone who comes near, even the dog. Grandpa backs away slowly. At snack time, she is <kanji>fierce</kanji>.
猛.on: Even the lawn <sound>mow</sound>er outside goes quiet when she glares at it.

壮.meaning: An old <part>gentleman</part> of ninety shins up the fire station's <part>climbing pole</part> every morning before his tea, then slides down and pours it. The young firefighters puff along behind him. He's still remarkably <kanji>robust</kanji>.
壮.on: At the top he washes his face with a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p, without slipping once.
壮.kun: His breakfast is one <sound>sa</sound>rdine, and a pink <sound>car</sound>nation in a vase for strength.

炉.meaning: In winter, the cottage <part>door</part> sneaks off its hinges at night and lies down by the <part>fire</part> like a big old dog, toes to the flames. By morning it's back in its frame, warm and smelling of smoke. Its favourite spot is the <kanji>hearth</kanji>.
炉.on: A little <sound>ro</sound>dent curls up on the doorknob to share the heat.
炉.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l in a <sound>ro</sound>cket-print scarf toasts a <sound>ree</sound>d over the glowing coals.

磨.meaning: A sculptor wants the perfect pebble, so she wraps a <part>stone</part> in rough <part>hemp</part> rope and drags it behind her bike for a thousand miles. When she unwraps it, it's a tiny marble, shiny as a mirror. Road and rope did the work to <kanji>grind</kanji> it down.
磨.on: She toasts the road with a big <sound>mu</sound>g of cocoa.
磨.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat buys the shiny pebble to polish his clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

秀.meaning: At the county fair, a stalk of <part>grain</part> pulls out a <part>folding ruler</part> to prove it's the tallest. It unfolds the ruler again and again, but the ruler runs out before the stalk does. The judges pin three ribbons on it. Some stalks just <kanji>excel</kanji>.
秀.on: The judges have to stand on a giant <sound>shoe</sound> to see the top.
秀.kun: One judge in high <sound>hee</sound>ls climbs all the way up to pin the ribbon.

憲.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part> of a garden shed, the vegetables hold a meeting. They write their rules on a <part>net</part>, plant it in the <part>soil</part>, and every sprout swears by its <part>heart</part>: no slugs, sunshine for all. That net becomes their <kanji>constitution</kanji>.
憲.on: The garden dog signs it too, from its <sound>ken</sound>nel, with a muddy paw.

稿.meaning: A farmer has no paper, so she writes her novel on <part>grain</part> stalks, one sentence per stalk, until the stack is as <part>tall</part> as the barn. Then the cows eat chapter three. 'Fine,' she says, 'it was only the first <kanji>draft</kanji>.'
稿.on: She writes chapter three again on an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, which also gets eaten.
稿.kun: The bare stalks she bundles for the cows, with a dab of <sound>wa</sound>sabi and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

殻.meaning: At a fancy picnic, a <part>gentleman</part> spreads a <part>blanket</part> over a little <part>table</part> and cracks a coconut for a curtseying <part>maiden</part>. She drinks the milk, then politely nibbles the whole hairy shell. He stares. 'The best part,' she says, 'is the <kanji>husk</kanji>.'
殻.on: Her dog gets the picked-clean <sound>carc</sound>ass of the roast chicken.
殻.kun: Her pet <sound>ca</sound>rp wears the last shell as a helmet, and the picnic cheers, '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'

懸.meaning: At the summer fair, every <part>prefecture</part> ties paper <part>heart</part> after paper heart along a rope of its <part>lineage</part>, one knot per grandparent, and strings it under the bridge. Hundreds of hearts dangle over the river, never touching the water. The rule is: <kanji>suspend</kanji> them all summer.
懸.on: A dog has strung its <sound>ken</sound>nel from the bridge too, and naps in it, swinging.
懸.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the river to look at the hanging hearts.

拘.meaning: A parrot keeps squawking one <part>phrase</part>, 'Stop, thief!', at a seagull who stole a chip. The harbour police chain the gull to a tiny <part>anchor</part> until the chip is returned. The parrot has made its first <kanji>arrest</kanji>.
拘.on: The gull pays its fine with a melting ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
拘.kun: After that the parrot won't get involved; it just watches a <sound>ca</sound>rp nap in a <sound>ca</sound>lm pond.

襲.meaning: On laundry day, a <part>sea serpent</part> bursts out of the harbour and charges the washing lines, grabbing every <part>garment</part> it can reach. Minutes later it's back on its rock, wearing six shirts and a bonnet. Fashion is why it chose to <kanji>attack</kanji>.
襲.on: For its last raid it steals one giant <sound>shoe</sound> and paddles off in it like a boat.
襲.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a lady, as it flops down on her <sound>so</sound>fa to show off the bonnet.

銅.meaning: A town orders a <part>gold</part> statue of its mayor and asks the sculptor to make it look the <part>same</part> as him. Ten years later it rains for a week, and the statue's nose turns green. The sculptor kept the gold and used <kanji>copper</kanji>.
銅.on: Now the bakery sells little mayors made of bread <sound>dough</sound>, green icing nose and all.
銅.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' says a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the fountain, and a <sound>ga</sound>rlic seller throws a <sound>ne</sound>t over the green nose.

賢.meaning: A palace <part>servant</part> must bring the queen a hot <part>shellfish</part> without burning her fingers. She threads a <part>pretzel</part> through the shell's hinge and carries it like a handbag, and the queen eats the handle as a snack. Promote that <kanji>intelligent</kanji> girl.
賢.on: Later she teaches the palace puppies to open their own <sound>ken</sound>nel.
賢.kun: Her pet <sound>ca</sound>rp, a <sound>shee</sound>p and a <sound>ko</sound>ala all line up to learn from her.

凝.meaning: A chef stares at his soup, full of <part>doubt</part>: did he add the salt? He wonders so long that the window frosts over and <part>ice</part> creeps across the bowl. When he finally tastes it, the soup won't pour. It has had time to <kanji>congeal</kanji>.
凝.on: He serves it anyway, sliced into cubes beside a plate of <sound>gyo</sound>za.
凝.kun: His <sound>ko</sound>ala kitchen helper rubs the chef's stiff shoulders.

伴.meaning: A lonely queen uses only one <part>half</part> of her royal <part>coat hook</part>; the other peg stays empty for years. One night a shy gardener hangs his muddy jacket there, next to her cape. The palace gasps, then cheers: the queen has a <kanji>consort</kanji>.
伴.on: At their wedding, the cake is dripping with <sound>hon</sound>ey.
伴.kun: He brings his <sound>to</sound>tem pole, his pet <sound>mo</sound>le and a basket of <sound>na</sound>an along with him.

姓.meaning: A <part>woman</part> labels every plant in her garden. Each new <part>life</part> that sprouts gets a tag, Tomato, Rose, Carrot, and then she adds Smith after it, because they're all family now. Everything in her garden shares her <kanji>surname</kanji>.
姓.on: She keeps the spare name tags locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe in the shed.

嫁.meaning: A <part>woman</part> marries a quiet beekeeper and moves into his family's <part>house</part>, where his eleven aunts live. By spring she runs the hives, the kitchen and the aunts. That's how it goes when you <kanji>marry into</kanji> a family.
嫁.on: Her wedding gift to them is a fat orange <sound>ca</sound>rp for the pond.
嫁.kun: Every morning the aunts bring the new bride a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

噴.meaning: At a quiet tea party, a shy librarian sips chilli tea by mistake. Her face turns red, her <part>mouth</part> trembles, and out shoots a <part>geyser</part> of steam that lifts the tablecloth and the cat. The guests duck. Spicy tea makes her <kanji>erupt</kanji>.
噴.on: The steam swirls round the room like a little ty<sound>phoon</sound>.
噴.kun: It blows the <sound>fu</sound>ton clean off the sofa and out of the window.

繁.meaning: An old knitter can't stop. With great <part>cleverness</part> she knits green <part>thread</part> into ivy, ferns and moss, until her flat is a jungle, a parrot moves in and the postman needs a machete. Her woollen garden is <kanji>luxuriant</kanji>.
繁.on: Wild bees build a hive in the wool and drip <sound>hon</sound>ey on the carpet.
繁.kun: <sound>Shee</sound>p wander in to graze, and a <sound>ge</sound>cko hides in the ferns.

殖.meaning: A museum skeleton is a few <part>bones</part> short, so the keeper lines up spares in a <part>straight</part> row and glues them on. Every night more appear. By Friday the dinosaur has three tails and a second neck. Someone keeps trying to <kanji>augment</kanji> it.
殖.on: The keeper gets such a <sound>shock</sound> each morning that her hair stands up.
殖.kun: She sleeps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton in the hall to catch whoever it is.
